title: Industrial Components
heading: Industrial components for your application
intro: Technical components selected around function, interfaces and operating conditions. We bring component selection, technical advice and sourcing together for your application.

overview.title: Component fields and selection requirements
overview.intro: Start with the function your equipment needs. Explore the component groups, then define the specifications, interfaces and quantities for a focused inquiry.

cards.title: Controllers & control systems
cards.text: Match control functions, inputs, outputs and installation requirements.
bullets: Define the control task and connections
Agree configuration and documentation

cards.title: Sensors & probes
cards.text: Define the measurement task and the connection to your equipment.
bullets: Specify range, installation and conditions
Agree the signal and required accuracy

cards.title: Heating elements
cards.text: Match the heating requirement, geometry and connection details to the application.
bullets: Define heating power and installation
Agree material and operating conditions

cards.title: Pressure & switching devices
cards.text: Clarify the switching function and the mechanical and electrical interfaces.
bullets: Define switching points and connections
Agree operating conditions and checks

selection.title: Define the component requirement
selection.intro: A part number, datasheet or application description is a useful starting point. We clarify the required characteristics before selecting a source.

cards.title: Function
cards.text: Describe the task, operating range and interaction with the equipment.

cards.title: Interfaces
cards.text: Specify installation space, mounting, connections and compatible signals.

cards.title: Operating conditions
cards.text: Identify temperature, media, environment and documentation requirements.

requirements.title: Match the component to the application
requirements.text: Selection brings function, interfaces and operating conditions together. Share existing references, drawings and any critical characteristics. We agree the component version, sample evaluation and documentation needed before release.

options.title: Selection and supply options
options.intro: Choose the route around the application and the information already available.

cards.title: Standard components
cards.text: Compare available component categories with the required function.

cards.title: Adapted components
cards.text: Discuss changes to geometry, interfaces or configuration.

cards.title: Replacement assessment
cards.text: Review an existing reference and the requirements for a suitable alternative.

cards.title: Recurring demand
cards.text: Define repeat quantities, delivery schedules and stock arrangements.

faqs.q: Can I start with an existing part number?
faqs.a: Yes. Share the reference, manufacturer information if available, and the application. Drawings, datasheets and quantities help clarify the requirement.

faqs.q: Where can I browse component categories?
faqs.a: The component catalogue groups controllers, sensors, heating elements and switching devices. Each category helps you prepare the relevant selection requirements.

faqs.q: Can a standard component be adapted?
faqs.a: Describe the required change and its purpose. We assess the technical scope and source options, then agree feasibility, samples and release requirements for the application.

title: Cable Assemblies
heading: Cable assemblies for your connections
intro: Custom cables and wiring harnesses matched to your equipment. Define connectors, pin assignments, cable lengths and operating conditions for an agreed assembly and checking scope.

overview.title: Cable assemblies and harness requirements
overview.intro: The connection task determines the cable, termination and routing requirements. Share drawings, connector references or a sample to define the assembly.

cards.title: Cable assemblies
cards.text: Prepare a defined connection between components or devices.
bullets: Specify connectors, pin assignments and length
Agree cable type, termination and strain relief

cards.title: Wiring harnesses
cards.text: Bring multiple connections and branches into a coordinated assembly.
bullets: Define branch lengths, routing and identification
Agree protection, fixing points and checks

selection.title: Cable and connection selection
selection.intro: Select the construction around the electrical task, installation and operating conditions. Specific materials and references are agreed for the assembly.

cards.title: Cable construction
cards.text: Define conductor count, cross-section, shielding and flexibility requirements.

cards.title: Connectors & contacts
cards.text: Specify mating references, contact assignment and termination details.

cards.title: Protection & routing
cards.text: Clarify sleeving, strain relief, bend space and installation conditions.

requirements.title: Define the connection and checking requirements
requirements.text: Record the wiring diagram, pin assignments, branch lengths and connector orientation. Agree continuity, insulation or other electrical checks where required, together with acceptance criteria, identification and documentation.

options.title: Assembly and delivery details
options.intro: Define the details that make the cable assembly ready for your installation.

cards.title: Identification
cards.text: Agree labels, part references and branch identification.

cards.title: Termination
cards.text: Define contact assembly and the required termination method.

cards.title: Protection
cards.text: Discuss sleeving, shielding connections and strain relief.

cards.title: Packing & supply
cards.text: Agree packaging, quantities and recurring delivery needs.

faqs.q: What information is needed for a cable assembly?
faqs.a: Provide connector references, a wiring diagram or pin list, cable lengths and quantities. Include the operating conditions and any electrical checks needed.

faqs.q: Can a sample be used as a starting point?
faqs.a: Yes. A sample can help clarify layout and interfaces. The agreed drawing, component references and checking criteria define the assembly to be supplied.

faqs.q: How are electrical checks agreed?
faqs.a: Specify the checks required for the application and the acceptance criteria. The scope, test records and responsibilities are confirmed with the offer.

cta: Have a cable or harness requirement?

title: Assembly & Subassemblies
heading: Assemblies ready for integration
intro: Mechanical and electromechanical assemblies coordinated around your interfaces. Define the parts, assembly requirements and functional checks for an agreed delivery condition.

overview.title: Assembly scope and integration requirements
overview.intro: Start with a bill of materials, assembly drawing or functional description. We clarify the supplied parts, interfaces and work needed for the subassembly.

cards.title: Mechanical assemblies
cards.text: Bring manufactured and purchased parts together as a defined unit.
bullets: Specify fits, fasteners and assembly sequence
Agree alignment, movement and dimensional checks

cards.title: Integration-ready subassemblies
cards.text: Coordinate mechanical interfaces and any electrical components needed for installation.
bullets: Define wiring, mounting and connection interfaces
Agree functional checks and delivery condition

selection.title: Define the assembly inputs
selection.intro: Clear part references and interface requirements create the basis for repeatable assembly and supply.

cards.title: Parts & references
cards.text: Provide the bill of materials, drawings and required revisions.

cards.title: Joining & mounting
cards.text: Specify fasteners, fits, joining requirements and any critical assembly settings.

cards.title: Electrical interfaces
cards.text: Define connections, routing, device references and functional requirements.

requirements.title: Agree how the assembly is assessed
requirements.text: Identify critical dimensions, movement, alignment and functional requirements. Agree the inspection scope, any application-specific tests and the records needed. Define the released assembly version and how changes are handled.

options.title: Preparation for installation and supply
options.intro: Specify the condition in which the assembly needs to reach your production or installation team.

cards.title: Parts coordination
cards.text: Agree which parts are sourced, supplied or provided by you.

cards.title: Assembly instructions
cards.text: Record the sequence, references and critical work steps.

cards.title: Functional checks
cards.text: Define the checks and acceptance criteria for the completed unit.

cards.title: Identification & packing
cards.text: Agree assembly references, protection and delivery units.

faqs.q: Can you work from a bill of materials?
faqs.a: Yes. Include part references, revisions, quantities and assembly drawings where available. We clarify missing interfaces and the scope of sourcing and assembly.

faqs.q: Can customer-supplied parts be included?
faqs.a: Discuss which parts you will provide and in what condition. Incoming checks, responsibility for shortages and the assembly scope are agreed for the project.

faqs.q: How are assembly changes handled?
faqs.a: Define the released drawings and bill of materials, then agree how proposed changes are reviewed, approved and reflected in subsequent deliveries.

title: Rubber & Silicone
heading: Rubber and silicone parts for your application
intro: Custom seals, membranes and molded elastomer components. Define geometry, material properties and operating conditions for a suitable tooling, sampling and production approach.

overview.title: Elastomer parts and requirements
overview.intro: The function and operating environment guide the material and geometry. Discuss the contact surfaces, movement and sealing requirements for your component.

cards.title: Seals & gaskets
cards.text: Define the geometry and contact conditions for sealing interfaces.
bullets: Specify dimensions, compression and mating surfaces
Agree material, hardness and evaluation criteria

cards.title: Membranes & molded parts
cards.text: Prepare custom flexible components around their installation and function.
bullets: Define movement, wall sections and fixing details
Agree tooling, samples and dimensional checks

selection.title: Material properties to define
selection.intro: Material family and compound selection are assessed against the application. The selected grade and required evidence are confirmed in the offer.

cards.title: Rubber compounds
cards.text: Discuss compound requirements for the intended media, temperature and mechanical loading.

cards.title: Silicone compounds
cards.text: Define the required flexibility, hardness, appearance and operating conditions.

cards.title: Application requirements
cards.text: Specify any contact, cleanliness, traceability or documentation requirements.

requirements.title: Define geometry and functional checks
requirements.text: Share drawings, sealing interfaces and the required hardness or other material properties. Agree the dimensions, sample evaluation and application-specific checks used to assess the component. Tooling and release conditions are defined before production.

options.title: Tooling and finishing details
options.intro: Clarify the details that affect the fit, appearance and assessment of the finished part.

cards.title: Tooling
cards.text: Agree the mold approach, parting lines and tool responsibilities.

cards.title: Surface & edges
cards.text: Specify flash limits, trimming and relevant contact surfaces.

cards.title: Color & identification
cards.text: Define color references and marking requirements where needed.

cards.title: Samples & release
cards.text: Agree sample quantities, evaluation criteria and approval records.

faqs.q: How is the elastomer material selected?
faqs.a: Start with the intended media, temperature, movement and sealing conditions. Specify required hardness and documentation so a suitable compound can be assessed.

faqs.q: Can parts be developed from a sample?
faqs.a: A sample can support the discussion. Geometry, material requirements and the criteria for evaluating a new component still need to be defined and agreed.

faqs.q: What should a sealing drawing include?
faqs.a: Show the part geometry, mating surfaces, installation space and critical dimensions. Include relevant compression, media and operating requirements.

cta: Have a rubber or silicone part requirement?

title: Die Casting
heading: Die casting for custom metal components
intro: Aluminum and zinc castings matched to your production requirements. Define alloy, geometry, tooling, machining and surface requirements from samples through recurring supply.

overview.title: Cast components and production requirements
overview.intro: The component geometry, alloy and expected quantities form the basis for the casting approach. We coordinate tooling, secondary operations and agreed checks.

cards.title: Custom castings
cards.text: Prepare the part geometry and functional requirements for a tooling review.
bullets: Define alloy, wall sections and critical interfaces
Agree tooling, samples and expected volumes

cards.title: Finished cast components
cards.text: Coordinate casting with machining and finishing for the required delivery condition.
bullets: Identify machined features and surface requirements
Agree dimensional checks and documentation

selection.title: Alloy and component selection
selection.intro: The specific alloy and process are assessed against the part. Material suitability and source availability are confirmed with the offer.

cards.title: Aluminum castings
cards.text: Discuss the alloy, geometry, machining and surface requirements for the component.

cards.title: Zinc castings
cards.text: Define material requirements, functional features and the required finish.

cards.title: Secondary operations
cards.text: Identify holes, threads, mating surfaces and other features requiring further work.

requirements.title: Agree casting and machining tolerances
requirements.text: Distinguish as-cast features from machined interfaces on the drawing. Define critical dimensions, surface requirements and any inspection needs. Tooling feasibility, sample assessment and release criteria are agreed for the specific component.

options.title: Tooling and finishing scope
options.intro: Include the operations needed to turn the casting into a component ready for your assembly.

cards.title: Tooling
cards.text: Define tool scope, ownership, maintenance and change requirements.

cards.title: Trimming & deburring
cards.text: Specify edge condition and the removal of process-related features.

cards.title: Machining
cards.text: Agree the final dimensions of holes, threads and mating surfaces.

cards.title: Surface finishing
cards.text: Discuss coating, appearance and functional surface requirements.

faqs.q: Which information is needed for a casting inquiry?
faqs.a: Provide a model or drawing, alloy requirements, quantities and critical interfaces. Include any machining, finish and inspection requirements.

faqs.q: Can machining be included after casting?
faqs.a: Yes. Identify the features that require machining and their final dimensions. The combined casting and machining scope is agreed in the offer.

faqs.q: How are tooling and samples handled?
faqs.a: Tool design, ownership, sampling and approval responsibilities are agreed before work proceeds. Samples are evaluated against the defined component requirements.

title: Extrusion
heading: Extruded profiles for your application
intro: Custom metal and plastic profiles with the required cutting, machining and finishing. Define the cross-section, material, lengths and interfaces for your component.

overview.title: Profiles and finishing requirements
overview.intro: Start with the profile drawing and its role in the assembly. The material, cross-section and secondary operations guide the manufacturing scope.

cards.title: Custom profiles
cards.text: Prepare the section geometry and metal or plastic material requirements for a custom profile.
bullets: Define cross-section, material and cut lengths
Agree tolerances, tooling and surface condition

cards.title: Cut & finished profiles
cards.text: Coordinate the profile with the secondary operations needed for installation.
bullets: Specify cut lengths, holes and local features
Agree finish, inspection and delivery condition

selection.title: Profile material and geometry
selection.intro: The material and section are selected together. Specific grades, tolerances and process suitability are assessed for the application.

cards.title: Metal requirements
cards.text: Define alloy, surface condition and the mechanical role of the profile.

cards.title: Plastic requirements
cards.text: Discuss rigidity, flexibility, appearance and the operating environment.

cards.title: Section & interfaces
cards.text: Show wall sections, channels, mating parts and critical dimensions.

requirements.title: Define profile tolerances and cut lengths
requirements.text: Identify critical cross-section dimensions, straightness, length and interface requirements. Agree tooling, sample assessment and the scope of any machining or finishing. Final specifications and checking criteria form part of the offer.

options.title: Secondary operations and delivery
options.intro: Coordinate the profile with the additional work required for your installation.

cards.title: Cutting
cards.text: Specify finished lengths, end condition and length tolerances.

cards.title: Machining
cards.text: Define holes, slots, threads and other local features.

cards.title: Finishing
cards.text: Agree surface appearance, coatings and protected interfaces.

cards.title: Packing & supply
cards.text: Define handling protection, delivery units and recurring quantities.

faqs.q: What should a profile drawing show?
faqs.a: Provide the complete cross-section, critical dimensions and the intended material. Include cut lengths, mating components and any secondary operations.

faqs.q: Can profiles be supplied cut and machined?
faqs.a: Yes. Define the finished lengths, local features and tolerances. Cutting, machining and finishing are included in the agreed scope.

faqs.q: How is a new profile assessed?
faqs.a: The material, section geometry and tooling requirements are reviewed for the intended application. Agree samples and checking criteria before release.

title: Sensors & Measurement
heading: Sensors and measurement for your application
intro: Sensors, probes and measurement components matched to the task. Define the measurement range, accuracy, installation and signal interfaces for your equipment.

overview.title: Measurement components and interfaces
overview.intro: Selection starts with what needs to be measured and how the result is used. Explore the component categories and clarify the connection to your equipment.

cards.title: Sensors & probes
cards.text: Match the sensing element, probe construction and connection to the application.
bullets: Define measurement range and operating conditions
Agree installation, signal and accuracy requirements

cards.title: Measurement integration
cards.text: Coordinate sensing with the receiving device and required connection.
bullets: Specify compatible inputs, outputs and wiring
Agree configuration, checks and documentation

selection.title: Selection parameters to define
selection.intro: A datasheet, existing reference or description of the measurement task provides a starting point for selection.

cards.title: Range & accuracy
cards.text: Define the measurement range, required accuracy and relevant evaluation conditions.

cards.title: Installation
cards.text: Specify probe dimensions, mounting, process connections and contact materials.

cards.title: Signal & connection
cards.text: Identify output requirements, supply, cable construction and connector references.

requirements.title: Agree the measurement and documentation scope
requirements.text: Define how the component is assessed in the intended application. Specify any calibration, traceability or test documentation you need. Required evidence, responsibilities and acceptance criteria are agreed for the selected component.

options.title: Configuration and integration details
options.intro: Bring the sensing component and its installation requirements together before the offer.

cards.title: Probe construction
cards.text: Define stem length, diameter, mounting and contact surfaces.

cards.title: Cables & connectors
cards.text: Match wiring, connector references and required cable lengths.

cards.title: Controls & readout
cards.text: Identify the receiving device and compatible signal interfaces.

cards.title: Documentation
cards.text: Agree identification, datasheets and any required measurement records.

faqs.q: What information helps select a sensor?
faqs.a: Describe the measurement task, range, required accuracy, mounting and operating conditions. Include the receiving device and any existing references.

faqs.q: Can probe geometry and cable connections be adapted?
faqs.a: Describe the required dimensions and interfaces. We assess the available or custom options, then agree the component specification and evaluation criteria.

faqs.q: Is calibration documentation included?
faqs.a: Specify the documentation and traceability requirements for your application. The available evidence and any agreed calibration scope are confirmed with the offer.

cta: Have a sensor or measurement requirement?

title: Vacuum Casting
heading: Vacuum casting for prototypes and small runs
intro: Cast polyurethane parts for prototype evaluation and small production runs. Define geometry, material properties, finish and quantities for a suitable master, mold and sampling approach.

overview.title: Prototype and small-run requirements
overview.intro: Start with a model or drawing and explain how the parts will be evaluated. Material properties and appearance requirements guide the casting scope.

cards.title: Prototype parts
cards.text: Prepare representative parts for fit, handling and agreed application checks.
bullets: Define geometry, interfaces and intended evaluation
Agree material properties, finish and samples

cards.title: Small production runs
cards.text: Plan a limited quantity around the agreed part and mold requirements.
bullets: Specify quantities and repeat requirements
Agree molds, checking criteria and delivery condition

selection.title: Material properties and master requirements
selection.intro: The casting material and master are selected around the part's intended use. Specific material characteristics and suitability are confirmed in the offer.

cards.title: Rigid polyurethane
cards.text: Define the required rigidity, appearance and functional properties.

cards.title: Flexible polyurethane
cards.text: Specify flexibility, hardness and the way the part will be evaluated.

cards.title: Master pattern
cards.text: Agree geometry, surface condition and the data needed to prepare the master.

requirements.title: Define the purpose of the cast part
requirements.text: Describe whether the part is intended for appearance, fit or functional evaluation. Agree the critical dimensions, material properties and checking conditions. The casting material must be assessed for the intended use; resemblance to another plastic does not establish equivalent performance.

options.title: Mold and finishing details
options.intro: Agree the production and finishing scope around the required quantity and delivery condition.

cards.title: Master & mold
cards.text: Define the master, parting approach and mold requirements.

cards.title: Appearance
cards.text: Agree color, texture and visible surface expectations.

cards.title: Inserts & interfaces
cards.text: Specify any inserts, connection features and mating components.

cards.title: Samples & repeat runs
cards.text: Agree sample evaluation, quantities and the scope of repeat orders.

faqs.q: What files are needed for a vacuum-casting inquiry?
faqs.a: Provide a model or drawing with critical dimensions, intended use, material-property requirements and quantities. Add appearance and finishing requirements where relevant.

faqs.q: Are cast polyurethane parts equivalent to injection-molded parts?
faqs.a: Material properties and process characteristics must be assessed for the intended use. A cast prototype should be evaluated against agreed requirements rather than assumed to match an injection-molded material.

faqs.q: Can small repeat runs be planned?
faqs.a: Discuss the expected quantities and timing alongside the mold and material requirements. The production scope, checking criteria and delivery conditions are confirmed in the offer.
